title: Slot-based metering and quota proration for late-binding KV cache fusion
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Late-binding cache fusion currently merges requests at the serving layer to maximize GPU utilization. Mixed microbatches can contain a blend of KV cache hits, prefix-cache hits, and cold misses (including speculative prefetches). Our current metering attributes the full aggregated token invoice to the microbatch originators in a simplistic way, which causes two classes of incorrect behavior: (1) overcharging when a hot tenant's KV hits subsidize cold tenants that are merged into the same fused microbatch; and (2) undercounting speculatively-prefetched tokens when they are amortized across many owners without a reproducible provenance. Additionally, rate limiter and quota windows are being consumed unevenly by fused batches which bypass per-tenant slot accounting, leading to noisy throttling and customer confusion.

Proposal: Implement a slot-based accounting model for late-binding fusion. Each incoming request reserves one or more logical "slots" representing its share of microbatch compute. When fusion occurs, the runtime will allocate token credits to slots based on observed provenance (explicit KV hit, cached prefix hit, miss, or speculative prefetch). Token costs and quota consumption will be prorated to the owning slots at emission time rather than attributing the entire fused batch to a single owner. For speculative prefetches we will record a separate "prefetch ledger" mapping tentative tokens to the originating tenant; if those tokens are later reused by other tenants in fused batches, we will apply a deterministic split heuristic to refund or reassign credits. This change also includes rate limiter integration: slot credits will consume per-tenant rate tokens and track loaned tokens for short-lived borrow scenarios, with reconciliation at microbatch commit.

Goals: produce correct, auditable per-tenant billing and quota behavior for fused microbatches; minimize cost variance for tenants with mixed hit/miss patterns; maintain low end-to-end latency by keeping accounting paths in the hot path but optimized and sampled for monitoring; provide a migration path that backfills historical ambiguity using sampling traces and logs where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Serving runtime emits logical slot IDs for every request entering the batching layer and includes slot provenance metadata for KV/prefix/prefetch status.
Billing pipeline can consume slot-level token-credit events and produces per-tenant token usage identical (within 1%) to a canonical non-fused baseline for synthetic workloads with mixed hits/misses.
Rate limiter accounts for slot loans and reconciles borrowings within the same formation window; no tenants observe unexplained quota drops after rollout in canary region.

Speculative prefetches are recorded to the prefetch ledger and either charged to the originator or deterministically split when reused by others; audit logs show the decision policy for at least 30 days.
End-to-end tests (unit + integration + e2e) cover representative fusion patterns: all-hit, all-miss, mixed, high-prefetch, and adversarial multi-tenant fusion.
Dashboard surfaces new metrics: slot_count, slot_utilization, slot_charge_split, prefetch_ledger_age, and observed refund rates; metrics ingestion is within existing quotas.
Migration script produces reconciled adjustments for customers with >5% historical variance and a clear communication plan exists for billing adjustments.
Performance overhead of slot accounting remains <4% p95 token latency on dedicated capacity in canary tests.
work_items: Draft design doc: slot accounting model, ledger schema, and reconciliation flows (Confluence link) - owner: Marco
Runtime change: emit slot IDs and provenance flags from batching layer; low-latency path implementation - owner: runtime team
Billing pipeline: ingest slot events, apply prorated splits, update aggregator and metering database - owner: billing team
Rate limiter integration: consume slot loans, implement reconciliation hook at microbatch commit - owner: infrastructure team
Prefetch ledger: schema, retention policy, and deterministic split heuristic implementation - owner: platform team
Backfill/migration script: sampling-based reconciliation for historical fused batches - owner: data infra
Tests: unit tests for accounting math, integration tests with fused microbatch emulator, e2e in canary region - owner: qa
Observability: dashboards, alerting thresholds, and smoke checks for rollout - owner: observability
Docs & customer comms: release notes, pricing FAQ updates, engineering runbook for incidents - owner: docs
notes: We should prefer deterministic heuristics for split decisions to keep refunds explainable in billing exports. Avoid expensive per-token provenance storage; use sampled trace ids for deep debug. Consider a future optimization that learns split ratios from historical co-occurrence instead of purely rule-based splits.
